Name: Hydrocarbons
Description: A compound consisting of carbon and hydrogen only.

Name: Cations
Description: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the proton.

Name: Anions
Description: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the electron.

Name: Carbonyl compouns: aldehydes or ketones
Description: carbonyl carbon C=O bonded only to H and/or carbon, spanning both aldehydes and ketones

Name: Aldehydes
Description: A compound RC(=O)H, in which a carbonyl group is bonded to one hydrogen atom and to one R group.

Name: Ketones
Description: A compound in which a carbonyl group is bonded to two carbon atoms: R2C=O (neither R may be H).

Name: Thiocarbonyl compounds: thioaldehydes or thioketones
Description: thiocarbonyl carbon C=S bonded to H/carbon, or a cumulated C=C=S thioketene carbon

Name: Thioaldehydes
Description: A compound in which the oxygen of an aldehyde has been replaced by divalent sulfur, RC(=S)H.

Name: Thioketones
Description: A thiocarbonyl compound in which the carbon of the thiocarbonyl group is bonded to two other carbon atoms, R2C=S (neither R may be H).

Name: Imines
Description: Compounds having the structure RN=CR2 (R = H, hydrocarbyl).

Name: Hydrazones
Description: Compounds having the structure R2C=NNR2, formally derived from aldehydes or ketones by replacing =O by =NNH2 (or substituted analogues).

Name: Semicarbazones
Description: A hydrazone resulting from the formal condensation of an aldehyde or ketone with the non-acylated nitrogen of semicarbazide or its substituted derivatives.

Name: Thiosemicarbazones
Description: A hydrazone resulting from the formal condensation of an aldehyde or ketone with the non-thioacylated nitrogen of thiosemicarbazide or its substituted derivatives.

Name: Oximes
Description: Compounds of structure R2C=NOH derived from condensation of aldehydes or ketones with hydroxylamine.

Name: Oxime ethers
Description: oxime ether: C=N-O-C, the oxime hydroxyl O-alkylated instead of left as free OH

Name: Ketenes
Description: Carbonyl compounds where the C=O bond is conjugated to an alkylidene group.

Name: Ketene acetal derivatives
Description: vinylidene carbon C=C bonded to two heteroatom substituents, as in ketene acetals or aminals

Name: Carbonyl hydrates
Description: gem-diol carbon: sp3 carbon bearing two hydroxyls, the hydrate of an aldehyde or ketone

Name: Hemiacetals / Hemiketals
Description: sp3 carbon bearing one hydroxyl and one ether oxygen on the same carbon (hemiacetal/hemiketal)

Name: Acetals / Ketals
Description: sp3 carbon bonded to two ether oxygens, C(OR)(OR'), i.e. two alkoxy groups on one carbon

Name: Hemiaminals
Description: Any organic amino compound that has an amino group and a hydroxy group attached to the same carbon atom.

Name: Aminals
Description: Compounds having two amino groups bonded to the same carbon, R2C(NR2)2.

Name: Thiohemiaminals
Description: sp3 carbon bearing both a thiol/thioether sulfur and an amino nitrogen on the same carbon

Name: Thioacetals / Thioketals
Description: sp3 carbon bonded to two thioether sulfurs, or one thioether sulfur and one ether oxygen

Name: Enamines
Description: An amine RNR'R'' where R has a double bond adjacent to the amine nitrogen.

Name: Enols
Description: Alkenols; the term refers specifically to vinylic alcohols, which have the structure HOCR'=CR2.

Name: Enolethers
Description: vinyl ether: C=C-O-C, an alkoxy group attached to an alkene carbon (enol ether)

Name: Hydroxy compounds: alcohols or phenols
Description: hydroxyl on any carbon, aliphatic or aromatic, excluding acetal-, hemiacetal- and acid-type oxygens

Name: Alcohols
Description: A compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom.

Name: Primary alcohols
Description: A primary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has either three hydrogen atoms attached to it or only one other carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms attached to it.

Name: Secondary alcohols
Description: A secondary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has two other carbon atoms attached to it.

Name: Tertiary alcohols
Description: A tertiary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has three other carbon atoms attached to it.

Name: 1,2-Diols
Description: two adjacent sp3 carbons each bearing a hydroxyl group (vicinal 1,2-diol)

Name: 1,2-Aminoalcohols
Description: adjacent sp3 carbons bearing a hydroxyl and an amino group (vicinal 1,2-amino alcohol)

Name: Phenols
Description: hydroxyl group attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (phenolic OH, ArOH)

Name: Diphenols
Description: benzene-type ring bearing two hydroxyl substituents (catechol/resorcinol/hydroquinone-type diphenol)

Name: Enediols
Description: C=C alkene bearing a hydroxyl on each of the two double-bond carbons (1,2-enediol)

Name: Ethers
Description: An organooxygen compound with formula ROR, where R is not hydrogen.

Name: Dialkylethers
Description: ether oxygen bonded to two saturated (sp3) carbons, R-O-R with no aryl or other heteroatom neighbor

Name: Alkylarylethers
Description: ether oxygen linking one sp3 alkyl carbon and one aromatic ring carbon (Ar-O-R)

Name: Diarylethers
Description: ether oxygen linking two aromatic ring carbons, Ar-O-Ar, excluding 3-membered-ring oxygens

Name: Thioethers
Description: Former name for sulfides RSR (R ≠ H).

Name: Disulfides
Description: Compounds of structure RSSR'.

Name: Peroxides
Description: Compounds of structure ROOR'.

Name: Hydroperoxides
Description: A monosubstitution product of hydrogen peroxide, HOOH.

Name: Hydrazine derivatives
Description: N-N single bond between two nitrogens each singly- or doubly-bonded to H/carbon (hydrazine linkage)

Name: Hydroxylamines
Description: Hydroxylamine, H2N‒OH, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives.

Name: Amines
Description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

Name: Primary aliphatic amines
Description: NH2 group attached to a saturated sp3 carbon that carries no other heteroatom

Name: Primary aromatic amines
Description: NH2 group attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (aniline-type primary amine)

Name: Secondary aliphatic amines
Description: NH bonded to two saturated sp3 carbons, neither carbon bearing another heteroatom

Name: Secondary mixed amines (aryl alkyl)
Description: NH bridging one aromatic ring carbon and one saturated sp3 carbon (N-alkylaniline)

Name: Secondary aromatic amines
Description: NH bonded to two aromatic ring carbons, Ar-NH-Ar (diarylamine, secondary aromatic amine)

Name: Tertiary aliphatic amines
Description: nitrogen bonded to three saturated sp3 carbons, none bearing another heteroatom (trialkylamine)

Name: Tertiary mixed amines (aryl alkyl)
Description: nitrogen bonded to one aromatic ring carbon and two sp3 carbons (N,N-dialkylaniline-type amine)

Name: Tertiary aromatic amines
Description: nitrogen bonded to three aromatic ring carbons (triarylamine)

Name: Quaternary ammonium salts
Description: Derivatives of ammonium compounds, (NH4+)Y−, in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with univalent (usually organyl) groups.

Name: N-Oxides
Description: nitrogen bearing an extra O- or =O beyond its normal valence (amine/imine/aromatic N-oxide)

Name: Halogen derivatives (alkyl, alkenyl, aryl)
Description: halogen (F/Cl/Br/I) on an sp3, alkene, or aromatic ring carbon, excluding acyl halides

Name: Alkyl fluorides
Description: fluorine on an sp3 carbon that is not allylic, propargylic or benzylic (fluoroalkane)

Name: Alkyl chlorides
Description: chlorine on an sp3 carbon that is not allylic, propargylic or benzylic (chloroalkane)

Name: Alkyl bromides
Description: bromine on an sp3 carbon that is not allylic, propargylic or benzylic (bromoalkane)

Name: Alkyl iodides
Description: iodine on an sp3 carbon that is not allylic, propargylic or benzylic (iodoalkane)

Name: Aryl fluorides
Description: fluorine attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (fluoroarene)

Name: Aryl chlorides
Description: chlorine attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (chloroarene)

Name: Aryl bromides
Description: bromine attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (bromoarene)

Name: Aryl iodides
Description: iodine attached directly to an aromatic ring carbon (iodoarene)

Name: Organometallic compounds
Description: A compound having bonds between one or more metal atoms and one or more carbon atoms of an organyl group.

Name: Organolithium compounds
Description: A compound containing at least one carbon-lithium bond.

Name: Organomagnesium compounds
Description: A compound containing at least one carbon-magnesium bond.

Name: Carboxylic acid derivatives
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded to a heteroatom substituent other than a thiol/thioether sulfur

Name: Carboxylic acids
Description: A carbon oxoacid acid carrying at least one ‒C(=O)OH group and having the structure RC(=O)OH, where R is any any monovalent functional group.

Name: Carboxylic acid salts
Description: carboxylate anion: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded to a negatively charged oxygen

Name: Carboxylic acid esters
Description: ester carbon: acyl C(=O) bonded to an ether-type oxygen that carries a carbon substituent

Name: Lactones
Description: Any cyclic carboxylic ester containing a 1-oxacycloalkan-2-one structure, or an analogue having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

Name: Carboxylic acid amides
Description: amide carbon: acyl C(=O) bonded to a nitrogen (primary, secondary or tertiary carboxamide)

Name: Carboxylic acid primary amides
Description: amide carbon C(=O) bonded to an unsubstituted NH2 group (primary carboxamide)

Name: Carboxylic acid secondary amides
Description: amide carbon C(=O) bonded to an NH bearing one carbon substituent (secondary/N-substituted amide)

Name: Carboxylic acid tertiary amides
Description: amide carbon C(=O) bonded to a nitrogen carrying two carbon substituents (N,N-disubstituted amide)

Name: Lactams
Description: Cyclic amides of amino carboxylic acids, having a 1-azacycloalkan-2-one structure, or analogues having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

Name: Carboxylic acid hydrazides
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded to a hydrazine nitrogen, R-C(=O)-NH-NH2-type link (carbohydrazide)

Name: Carboxylic acid azides
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded directly to an azide group -N3 (acyl azide)

Name: Hydroxamic acids
Description: A compound, RkE(=O)lNHOH, derived from an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH) (l ≠ 0) by replacing ‒OH with ‒NHOH, and derivatives thereof.

Name: Carboxylic acid amidines
Description: amidine carbon flanked by an imine nitrogen and an amine nitrogen, C(=N-)-NR2 (carboxamidine)

Name: Carboxylic acid amidrazones
Description: amidine-like carbon in a C(=N-)-N-N chain, the hydrazine analogue of an amidine (amidrazone)

Name: Nitriles
Description: A compound having the structure RC≡N; thus a C-substituted derivative of hydrocyanic acid, HC≡N.

Name: Acyl halides
Description: A compound consisting of an acyl group bonded to halogen.

Name: Acyl fluorides
Description: A compound consisting of an acyl group bonded to fluorine.

Name: Acyl chlorides
Description: A compound consisting of an acyl group bonded to chlorine.

Name: Acyl bromides
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded directly to bromine (carboxylic acid bromide)

Name: Acyl iodides
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded directly to iodine (carboxylic acid iodide)

Name: Acyl cyanides
Description: acyl carbon C(=O) bonded directly to a nitrile carbon, R-C(=O)-C#N (acyl cyanide)

Name: Imido esters
Description: imidate carbon C(=NR)-OR', the O-alkylated form of an amide (imino ether)

Name: Imidoyl halides
Description: imidoyl carbon C(=NR)-X bonded to a halogen, the imine analogue of an acyl halide

Name: Thiocarboxylic acid derivatives
Description: acyl carbon: a C=S bonded to any heteroatom, or a C=O bonded to sulfur (thiocarboxylic acid family)

Name: Thiocarboxylic acids
Description: An organic acid in which one or both oxygens of a carboxy group have been replaced by divalent sulfur.

Name: Thiocarboxylic acid esters
Description: thioester carbon: C(=S)-O/S-C or C(=O)-S-C, an ester with sulfur replacing one oxygen

Name: Thiolactones
Description: A cyclic thioester of a mercapto carboxylic acid, containing a 1-thiacycloalkan-2-one structure, or an analogue having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

Name: Thiocarboxylic acid amides
Description: thioamide carbon C(=S) bonded to a nitrogen (thiocarboxamide)

Name: Thiolactams
Description: cyclic thioamide: ring carbon C(=S) bonded to a ring nitrogen (thiolactam)

Name: Imidothioesters
Description: imidothioate carbon C(=NR)-S-C, the sulfur analogue of an imidate (thioimidate)

Name: Oxohetarenes
Description: aromatic ring carbon with an exocyclic C=O near a ring NH/NR, O or S (e.g. pyridinone, aromatic pyranone)

Name: Thioxohetarenes
Description: aromatic ring carbon with an exocyclic C=S near a ring NH/NR, O or S (thio analogue of an oxohetarene)

Name: Iminohetarenes
Description: aromatic ring carbon with an exocyclic C=N near a ring NH/NR, O or S (imino analogue of an oxohetarene)

Name: Orthocarboxylic acid derivatives
Description: sp3 carbon bonded to one C/H and three heteroatom substituents (general orthoester/orthoamide carbon)

Name: Carboxylic acid orthoesters
Description: sp3 carbon bonded to three ether-type oxygens, C(OR)3 (orthoester carbon)

Name: Carboxylic acid amide acetals
Description: sp3 carbon bonded to two ether oxygens and an amino nitrogen, C(OR)2-NR2 (amide acetal/orthoamide)

Name: Carboxylic acid anhydrides
Description: two acyl carbons C(=O) bridged by a single ether-type oxygen (carboxylic acid anhydride)

Name: Carboxylic acid imides
Description: nitrogen flanked by two acyl carbons, C(=O)-N-C(=O) (carboxylic acid imide linkage)

Name: Carboxylic acid unsubstituted imides
Description: imide nitrogen bearing one hydrogen, flanked by two acyl carbons, R-CO-NH-CO-R (unsubstituted imide)

Name: Carboxylic acid substituted imides
Description: imide nitrogen bearing a carbon substituent (no H), flanked by two acyl carbons (N-substituted imide)

Name: CO2 derivative (general)
Description: carbon bonded only to heteroatom substituents via single, double or triple bonds (general CO2-type carbon)

Name: Carbonic acid derivatives
Description: acyl-type carbon C(=O) bonded to two oxygen (or halogen) substituents, the carbonic-acid family

Name: Carbonic acid monoesters
Description: carbonate-type carbon: HO-C(=O)-O-R, one hydroxyl and one alkoxy oxygen (carbonic acid monoester)

Name: Carbonic acid diesters
Description: carbonate carbon C(=O) bonded to two ether-type oxygens, RO-C(=O)-OR' (carbonic acid diester)

Name: Carbonic acid ester halides
Description: carbonate carbon C(=O) bonded to one ether oxygen and one halogen, RO-C(=O)-X (chloroformate-type)

Name: Thiocarbonic acid derivatives
Description: thiocarbonate-family carbon: C(=S) with two heteroatom substituents, or C(=O) with a sulfur substituent

Name: Thiocarbonic acid monoesters
Description: monoester of thiocarbonic acid: C(=O/S) bonded to a free OH or SH and one O/S-alkyl group

Name: Thiocarbonic acid diesters
Description: diester of thiocarbonic acid: a carbonyl/thiocarbonyl carbon flanked by two O/S-alkyl groups

Name: Thiocarbonic acid ester halides
Description: acid halide of a thiocarbonic acid ester: C(=O/S) bonded to one O/S-alkyl group and a halogen

Name: Carbamic acid derivatives
Description: carbamoyl group N-C(=O)-X, X any heteroatom besides carbon or sulfur (ester O, halide, N)

Name: Carbamic acid
Description: carbamic acid unit HO-C(=O)-N< (acid form of a carbamate), matched anywhere in a molecule

Name: Carbamic acid esters (urethanes)
Description: carbamate ester: alkyl-O-C(=O)-N, the alkoxycarbonylamino (urethane) linkage

Name: Carbamic acid halides
Description: carbamoyl halide: halogen-C(=O)-N, the acid-halide form of a carbamic acid

Name: Thiocarbamic acid derivatives
Description: thiocarbamoyl group N-C(=S)-X (halide, O or S) or N-C(=O)-S, a thiocarbamic acid derivative

Name: Thiocarbamic acids
Description: thiocarbamic acid: HO/HS-C(=S)-N or HS-C(=O)-N, the free O- or S-thio acid form of carbamic acid

Name: Thiocarbamic acid esters
Description: ester of a thiocarbamic acid: alkyl-O/S-C(=S)-N or alkyl-S-C(=O)-N

Name: Thiocarbamic acid halides
Description: thiocarbamoyl halide: halogen-C(=S)-N, the acid-halide form of a thiocarbamic acid

Name: Ureas
Description: urea group: two amine nitrogens joined through a carbonyl carbon, N-C(=O)-N

Name: Isoureas
Description: A carboximidic acid that is the imidic acid tautomer of urea, H2NC(=NH)OH, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives.

Name: Thioureas
Description: Compounds of general formula RR'NC(=S)NR''R'''.

Name: Isothioureas
Description: isothiourea: N-C(=N)-S-alkyl, the S-alkylated imino tautomer of a thiourea

Name: Guanidines
Description: guanidine unit: carbon double-bonded to one nitrogen, single-bonded to two others, anywhere in a molecule

Name: Semicarbazides
Description: semicarbazide unit N-C(=O)-N-N (hydrazinecarboxamide), excluding fused diacylhydrazide and hydrazone forms

Name: Thiosemicarbazides
Description: thiosemicarbazide: N-C(=S)-NH-NH2 skeleton, a thiourea with one amino replaced by hydrazine

Name: Azides
Description: Any nitrogen molecular entity containing the group ‒N3.

Name: Azo compounds
Description: Derivatives of diazene with the general structure R‒N=N‒R'.

Name: Diazonium salts
Description: Compounds of structure RN2+Y−, in which R is generally but not necessarily aryl, and the cations of which are usually formulated as RN+≡N.

Name: Isonitriles
Description: isocyanide (isonitrile) group: a carbon attached to a terminal N#C isocyanide nitrogen

Name: Cyanates
Description: Salts and esters of cyanic acid, HOC≡N; compounds carrying the cyanate functional group -O-C≡N.

Name: Isocyanates
Description: Organonitrogen compounds that are derivatives of isocyanic acid; compounds containing the isocyanate functional group ‒N=C=O (as opposed to the cyanate group, -O-C≡N).

Name: Thiocyanates
Description: Esters of thiocyanic acid with general formula RSC≡N.

Name: Isothiocyanates
Description: An organosulfur compound with the general formula R‒N=C=S.

Name: Carbodiimides
Description: Any organonitrogen compound that consists of two primary amino groups joined to a central carbon atom via N=C linkages.

Name: Nitroso compounds
Description: Compounds having the nitroso group, ‒NO, attached to carbon, or to another element, most commonly nitrogen or oxygen.

Name: Nitro compounds
Description: A compound having a nitro group, ‒NO2 (free valence on nitrogen), which may be attached to carbon, nitrogen (as in nitramines), or oxygen (as in nitrates), among other elements (in the absence of specification, C-nitro compounds are usually implied).

Name: Nitrites
Description: Salts and esters of nitrous acid, HONO.

Name: Nitrates
Description: Salts or esters of nitric acid.

Name: Sulfuric acid derivatives
Description: S(=O)2 sulfur flanked by two heteroatoms (not C/H): generalizes sulfamate, sulfamide, sulfate ester

Name: Sulfuric acid
Description: sulfate/sulfuric-acid-ester fragment HO-S(=O)(=O)-O- (or ionized), matched as a substituent anywhere

Name: Sulfuric acid monoesters
Description: monoester of sulfuric acid: alkyl-O-SO2-OH, one ester oxygen and one free acid oxygen

Name: Sulfuric acid diesters
Description: diester of sulfuric acid (dialkyl sulfate): two alkoxy groups on the SO2 sulfur

Name: Sulfuric acid amide esters
Description: sulfamate ester: alkyl-O-SO2-N, one ester oxygen and one amino group on the sulfate sulfur

Name: Sulfuric acid amides
Description: sulfamic acid group: HO-SO2-N, a free hydroxy/oxo and an amino group on the same sulfur

Name: Sulfuric acid diamides
Description: sulfamide: N-SO2-N, two amino groups on a single sulfuric-acid-type sulfur

Name: Sulfuryl halides
Description: sulfuryl halide: a halogen and another heteroatom substituent on an S(=O)2 sulfur

Name: Sulfonic acid derivatives
Description: sulfonyl group R-SO2-X: a carbon-bonded S(=O)2 sulfur attached to a heteroatom (O, N, halide)

Name: Sulfonic acids
Description: sulfonic acid: a carbon-bonded S(=O)2-OH group (or its anion)

Name: Sulfonic acid esters
Description: sulfonate ester: a carbon-bonded S(=O)2-O-alkyl group

Name: Sulfonamides
Description: An amide of a sulfonic acid RS(=O)2NR'2.

Name: Sulfonyl halides
Description: sulfonyl halide: a carbon-bonded S(=O)2 sulfur attached to a halogen

Name: Sulfones
Description: sulfone-type sulfur: two carbons on a hexavalent S double-bonded twice to O, S or N

Name: Sulfoxides
Description: An organosulfur compound having the structure R2S=O or R2C=S=O (R ≠ H).

Name: Sulfinic acid derivatives
Description: sulfinyl group R-S(=O)-X: a carbon-bonded tervalent sulfoxide-type sulfur attached to a heteroatom

Name: Sulfinic acids
Description: sulfinic acid: a carbon-bonded S(=O)-OH group (or its anion)

Name: Sulfinic acid esters
Description: sulfinate ester: a carbon-bonded S(=O)-O-alkyl group

Name: Sulfinic acid halides
Description: sulfinyl halide: a carbon-bonded S(=O) sulfur attached to a halogen

Name: Sulfinic acid amides
Description: sulfinamide: a carbon-bonded S(=O)-N group, the nitrogen not itself part of an amide

Name: Sulfenic acid derivatives
Description: sulfenyl group R-S-X: a divalent, carbon-bonded sulfur attached to a heteroatom other than sulfur

Name: Sulfenic acids
Description: sulfenic acid: a carbon-bonded divalent sulfur single-bonded to a hydroxy group, C-S-OH

Name: Sulfenic acid esters
Description: sulfenate ester: a carbon-bonded divalent sulfur bonded to an alkoxy group, C-S-O-C

Name: Sulfenic acid halides
Description: sulfenyl halide: a carbon-bonded divalent sulfur attached to a halogen

Name: Sulfenic acid amides
Description: sulfenamide: a carbon-bonded divalent sulfur attached to a nitrogen, C-S-N

Name: Thiols
Description: An organosulfur compound in which a thiol group, ‒SH, is attached to a carbon atom of any aliphatic or aromatic moiety.

Name: Alkylthiols
Description: aliphatic thiol: a non-aromatic sp3/sp2 carbon bonded to -SH, excluding thioamide/thioacid carbons

Name: Thiophenols
Description: thiol (-SH) bonded directly to an aromatic ring carbon (arenethiol), anywhere in a molecule

Name: Phosphoric acid derivatives
Description: phosphoryl O=P with three non-carbon substituents (H, O, N or halide): a phosphoric acid derivative

Name: Phosphoric acids
Description: Compounds containing one or more phosphoric acid units.

Name: Phosphoric acid esters
Description: phosphate ester: phosphoryl O=P bonded to one alkoxy group and two other non-carbon substituents

Name: Phosphoric acid halides
Description: phosphoryl halide: O=P bonded to a halogen and two other non-carbon substituents

Name: Phosphoric acid amides
Description: phosphoramidate: phosphoryl O=P bonded to an amino nitrogen and two other non-carbon groups

Name: Thiophosphoric acid derivatives
Description: thiophosphoryl group: P(=S) or P(=O)(-S-) core with three non-carbon substituents

Name: Thiophosphoric acids
Description: thiophosphoric acid: P(=S or =O) bonded to a free OH or SH and two other O/S groups

Name: Thiophosphoric acid esters
Description: ester of a thiophosphoric acid: P(=S or =O) bonded to an alkyl O/S ester and two other groups

Name: Thiophosphoric acid halides
Description: acid halide of a thiophosphoric acid: P(=S or =O) bonded to a halogen and two other groups

Name: Thiophosphoric acid amides
Description: amide of a thiophosphoric acid: P(=S or =O) bonded to an amino nitrogen and two other groups

Name: Phosphonic acid derivatives
Description: phosphonyl group: O=P bonded to one carbon and two other non-carbon substituents

Name: Phosphonic acids
Description: HP(=O)(OH)2 (phosphonic acid) and its P-substituted derivatives.

Name: Phosphonic acid esters
Description: ester of a phosphonic acid: O=P bonded directly to carbon, an alkoxy group, and one other heteroatom

Name: Phosphines
Description: Phosphane (PH3) and compounds derived from it by substituting one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups: RPH2, R2PH, R3P (R ≠ H) are called primary, secondary and tertiary phosphines, respectively.

Name: Phosphinoxides
Description: phosphine oxide: a pentavalent phosphorus double-bonded to O and singly bonded to three carbons

Name: Boronic acid derivatives
Description: boronyl group: a trivalent boron bonded to one carbon and two other non-carbon substituents

Name: Boronic acids
Description: Compounds having the structure RB(OH)2.

Name: Boronic acid esters
Description: ester of a boronic acid: trivalent boron bonded to carbon, an alkoxy group, and H or another heteroatom

Name: Alkynes
Description: carbon-carbon triple bond C#C between two sp carbons, matched anywhere it occurs, fused or acyclic

Name: Aromatic compounds
Description: A cyclically conjugated molecular entity with a stability (due to delocalization) significantly greater than that of a hypothetical localized structure (e.g. Kekulé structure) is said to possess aromatic character.

Name: Arenes
Description: six-membered all-carbon aromatic ring (benzene), matched even when fused into larger polycyclic systems

Name: Heterocyclic compounds
Description: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of at least two different elements.

Name: Aromatic heterocyclic compounds
Description: aromatic heteroatom in a ring: any non-carbon ring atom that is part of an aromatic system

Name: α-Hydroxyacids
Description: alpha-hydroxy acid: a carboxylic acid HO-C(=O)- with a hydroxy group on the adjacent sp3 carbon

Name: 1,2-Diamines
Description: 1,2-diamine: amino nitrogens on two adjacent sp3 carbons, neither nitrogen part of an amidine/imine

Name: 1,2-Dithiols
Description: 1,2-dithiol: thiol groups (-SH) on two adjacent sp3 carbons

Name: 1,2-Aminothiols
Description: 1,2-aminothiol: a thiol and an amino group on two adjacent sp3 carbons

Name: α-Oxoacids
Description: alpha-keto acid: a carboxylic acid HO-C(=O)- adjacent to a second carbonyl carbon, C(=O)-C(=O)

Name: α, β-Unsaturated carboxylic acids
Description: alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid: HO-C(=O)- conjugated to a C=C double bond

Name: Dithiophenols
Description: benzenedithiol: an aromatic ring carbon bearing -SH, with a second ring carbon also bearing -SH

Name: Aminophenols
Description: A substituted aniline carrying a hydroxy substituent.

Name: Aminothiophenols
Description: aminothiophenol: an aromatic ring carbon bearing -SH, with an amino group on another ring carbon

Name: Aryl halides
Description: aryl halide: a halogen bonded directly to an aromatic ring carbon

Name: Alkyl halides
Description: haloalkane: a halogen on an sp3 carbon that is not allylic, propargylic, or benzylic

Name: Primary amines
Description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one hydrogen atom by a hydrocarbyl group.

Name: Secondary amines
Description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

Name: Tertiary amines
Description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

Name: Thiocarbonic acid esters
Description: ester of a thiocarbonic acid: a carbonyl/thiocarbonyl carbon bonded to at least one O/S-alkyl group

Name: Acid anhydrides
Description: Compounds consisting of two acyl groups bonded to the same oxygen atom acyl‒O‒acyl.
